events.title: If the Good Lord's Willing and the Creek Don't Rise
events.time: 7:00 PM · Manitou Opera House, 325 Main Street, Manitou, MB
events.description: This zany comedy, in the spirit of Kaufman and Hart, centers on Doc, an eccentric old man whose house caters to all sorts of characters. Now a retired judge, he spends his days “enjoying life.” When he’s not flying around the countryside in his balloon or fishing in a nearby dry riverbed, he works on his books of nonsense. This prompts his daughter, Charlotte, to decide he’s lost his marbles. So, conspiring with a sly lawyer, she plans to not only become his guardian but also sell his house and property. Throw in a psychologist on her first case, love sick teenagers, an irate school bus driver and an occasional artist or two and it’s a madhouse! Will Doc be committed or not? Of course he offers his own defense. “You ought to try tilting at a windmill every so often,” he philosophizes. “It’s great exercise and a nice breeze goes with it.” When he shows up at his sanity hearing dressed as a magician, his daughter and her lawyer think they have it all sewed up. However, Doc has a few surprise rabbits to pull out of the hat. This tour de force is appropriate for all audiences. Can Doc pull it off? As Leo says, “There is method to his madness.” And Doc shows one and all what a little nonsense can do “If the Good Lord’s Willing and the Creek Don’t Rise.” Performed by Candlewick's Manitou & Region Sr. High Drama Troupe.

events.description: After packing the house with a sold-out performance in November 2025, The Sharpe Brothers Band is making a highly anticipated return to the Manitou Opera House this November - this time for two performances of Another Night of Country Music. And before anyone asks - no, they're not all brothers. The Sharpe Brothers Band features brothers Will Sharpe (vocals/guitar) and James Sharpe (vocals/bass), along with Charlie Howatt (steel guitar), Gil Dudgeon (drums), and Larry Martineau (fiddle/harmonica). A performance at the Manitou Opera House with The Sharpe Brothers Band offers a timeless country music experience reminiscent of the Grand Ole Opry, right here in southern Manitoba. Audiences can expect a show filled with traditional country music, honky-tonk favourites, outstanding musicianship, a few surprises, and the warm, intimate atmosphere that has made the historic Manitou Opera House one of southern Manitoba's premier live music venues. Their 2025 appearance at the Manitou Opera House sold out well in advance, leaving many hoping for another opportunity to experience the band live. In response to the demand, the Manitou Opera House Foundation is thrilled to welcome them back for not one, but two unforgettable showings of country music, offering audiences the opportunity to attend either - or both - shows. With last year's performance selling out, early ticket purchases are strongly encouraged. Thank you to our event sponsors: Manitou Thrift Store, Dead Horse Cider Co., and Blumstein Brewing Co. events.description: International violin sensation and five-time Gospel Music Award winner Rosemary Siemens has performed four times at New York's Carnegie Hall, made history as the first violinist to perform at the Sistine Chapel at the Vatican, and taken the stage at the Grand Ole Opry. With over 200 million YouTube views, Rosemary's Sunday Hymn Serenade - Bring Back the Hymns has become one of the world's leading hymn channels. Her career spans more than 25 countries and 40 U.S. states, including performances for two U.S. presidents and Canadian prime ministers. Her honors include Country/Gospel Album of the Year at Canada's Gospel Music Awards. Now, experience her music live in A Bring Back the Hymns Christmas, featuring her husband, internationally award-winning saxophonist Eli Bennett, and their family. Together as SaxAndViolin, Rosemary and Eli will share the Christmas carols and beloved hymns you love, with Rosemary singing and playing violin, Eli on saxophone, and special family performances. Rosemary will also share inspiring stories from her international musical journey and the faith that has guided it. Bring your children, parents, grandparents, and friends. Come sing along, make Christmas memories together, and celebrate the birth of Jesus! CONCERT DETAILS Friday, December 4, 2026 Emmanuel Mennonite Church 750 Fifteenth Street Winkler, Manitoba, Canada 7 PM: Concert FREE admission. No tickets required. Limited seating. events.title: Mark Humphries Orchestra Christmas Show
events.time: 2:00 PM · Manitou Opera House, 325 Main Street, Manitou, MB
events.description: Swing into the holiday season at the Manitou Opera House! Get into the Christmas spirit with an afternoon of festive music, big band swing, Christmas favourites and plenty of laughs when the Mark Humphries Orchestra takes the stage at the historic Manitou Opera House. From classic big band sounds to the holiday songs you know and love, this special Christmas performance promises an afternoon filled with music, memories and Christmas cheer. Whether you're a longtime fan of big band music or looking for a fun and festive way to celebrate the season, the Mark Humphries Orchestra is sure to put a swing in your Christmas step! Sunday, December 13, 2026 2:00 PM Doors open at 1:30 PM Manitou Opera House — Manitou, Manitoba About the Mark Humphries Orchestra Originally from Yorkshire, England, Mark Humphries comes from a family where music and entertainment run deep. His father, Dick Van Winkle, toured the world as a multi-instrumental comedic entertainer. Mark's own musical journey began at the age of 13 when his trumpet teacher invited him to sit in with a local swing band called Sounds 40. That early experience eventually led to performances with the UK's premier big band, the Syd Lawrence Orchestra. The original Mark Humphries Orchestra was formed in 1987 and toured throughout the United Kingdom until Mark and his wife, Jill, emigrated with their family to Western Manitoba in 2008. After settling in Manitoba, Mark returned to performing with the Brandon-based Scotty McIntosh Big Band. Following McIntosh's retirement, Mark took over as leader and reinvented the ensemble, bringing together talented musicians from Brandon University, Winnipeg, Shilo, Melita, Swan River and Saskatchewan. Today, Humphries proudly carries on the family tradition of combining music and comedy, bringing audiences the Canadian version of the Mark Humphries Orchestra. A Christmas Afternoon of Music & Laughter For this special Christmas performance, audiences can expect the orchestra to put its own swinging spin on the holiday season. Come enjoy an afternoon of: Big band swing Christmas favourites Classic music Mark Humphries' signature comedy A festive afternoon at the historic Manitou Opera House Bring your family, friends or fellow music lovers and swing into the holiday season with us!
